items.title: Geometric irreducibility is equivalent to irreducibility of the self product
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes geometric irreducibility of a scheme X over a field k by irreducibility of the self product X times_k X (statement lines 1486-1490). One direction is a consequence of the base change behaviour of irreducible components. The converse is the interesting half and runs by contradiction through the function field: after replacing X by its reduced structure one knows X is irreducible, hence integral; assuming there is a separably algebraic element alpha of the function field outside k, one chooses a nonempty affine open U with k contained in E = k(alpha) contained in O(U), so that E tensor_k E sits inside O(U times U) and one gets a dominant morphism to the spectrum of E tensor E; irreducibility of the self product then makes that spectrum connected (proof lines 1492-1512). But if E were bigger than k, its tensor square would be a product of at least two fields, since as a k-vector space it has dimension the square of dim_k(E), contradicting connectedness; hence E = k and the function field criterion gives geometric irreducibility (proof lines 1513-1520). The claim is H2: one reduction, one dominant-morphism argument and a short dimension count.
